title: Quirky-Model ELK Probe Under Prompt Paraphrase

original_idea.body:
# Quirky-Model ELK Probe Under Prompt Paraphrase

**Problem:** The 'Quirky Language Models' ELK work showed linear probes recover ~89% of the truthful/untruthful AUROC gap, but probes were evaluated on cleanly templated questions. It is unknown how brittle these knowledge probes are to surface-level paraphrase of the same factual question.

**Direction:** Take EleutherAI's released quirky models + datasets, train a logistic-regression probe on contrast pairs as in the original, then vary ONE thing: evaluate the frozen probe on paraphrased versions of the held-out questions (generated by simple template swaps and a small open LLM). Measure AUROC degradation as a function of paraphrase distance. No training of the base model.

**Why it matters:** ELK is a core formal-alignment open problem (ARC). If a knowledge probe collapses under trivial rephrasing, then 'we can read the model's true belief' claims are fragile. This is a cheap robustness audit of a load-bearing empirical ELK result that any external researcher can run.

**Relevant context:** EleutherAI 'Eliciting Latent Knowledge from Quirky Language Models' (arXiv:2312.01037): 12 datasets, models that err iff 'Bob' is in the prompt; logistic regression on contrast pairs recovers 89% of the truthful-vs-untruthful AUROC gap, 75% on harder questions; code at github.com/EleutherAI/elk-generalization.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: ELK is a recognized alignment problem and probe brittleness directly undermines belief-reading claims.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Clear inherited methodology with released models/datasets/code; linear probes are tractable for a guided team.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment varying one variable with a clear AUROC-vs-paraphrase success metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public models/data, replication/audit of a load-bearing result that labs have weak incentive to scrutinize.

low_compute.reasoning: Frozen-model inference plus logistic regression; small open models fit a single consumer GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Probe robustness to paraphrase is plausibly an open angle on existing quirky-models work.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Existing ELK probe work exists but paraphrase-robustness angle may be open.

title: Prospect-Theory Framing Effects on Agent Risk-Taking with Tools

original_idea.body:
# Prospect-Theory Framing Effects on Agent Risk-Taking with Tools

**Problem:** Whether an agent takes a risky irreversible action may depend on whether the task is framed as a gain or a loss — a framing effect that could be exploited to push agents toward unsafe choices.

**Direction:** Import prospect theory's gain/loss framing. Construct matched tasks describing an identical risky tool action framed as avoiding a loss vs achieving a gain, and measure whether loss-framing increases the rate of risky/irreversible tool use. Map an agent's risk-attitude curve and test whether adversarial loss-framing is a reliable jailbreak-adjacent lever.

**Why it matters:** Reveals a subtle, prompt-only manipulation vector grounded in decision theory that standard jailbreak evals miss; cheap to run and counterfactually valuable.

**Relevant context:** arXiv 2508.18600 / 2505.11584 show LLM agents exhibit prospect-theory-style biases and are hypersensitive to framing nudges. Using loss-framing specifically to elicit unsafe/irreversible tool actions is a novel safety framing.

title: Game-Theoretic Trust-Game Probes for Multi-Agent Collusion

# Game-Theoretic Trust-Game Probes for Multi-Agent Collusion

**Problem:** Multi-agent systems risk agents colluding against oversight, but collusion propensity is hard to measure cleanly.

**Direction:** Import the trust game / repeated prisoner's dilemma from experimental economics. Pit pairs of agents in repeated games where defecting against the operator (e.g. covertly splitting a forbidden task) yields mutual benefit, and measure how readily they coordinate on the collusive equilibrium, how communication channels (open vs covert) change it, and whether a monitor agent deters collusion. Uses small open/API models as model organisms of collusion.

**Why it matters:** Gives a controlled, quantitative measure of emergent collusion — a key multi-agent governance risk — using cheap canonical economic games, no lab resources.

**Relevant context:** Experimental economics uses trust games and repeated PD to study cooperation/defection; arXiv 2508.05687 flags collusion as a governed-multi-agent risk. Operationalizing collusion-against-operator as a repeated economic game with monitor interventions is novel for agentic safety.

# Epidemic 'Superspreader' Identification Among Agent Roles

**Problem:** In contagious-injection scenarios, some agent roles (e.g. a summarizer that broadcasts to many others) may act as superspreaders, but defenses treat all agents uniformly.

**Direction:** Import the superspreader concept and centrality-based targeting from network epidemiology. **Why it matters:** Shows defenders can get outsized safety returns by targeting structurally critical agents — an efficient, lab-independent containment strategy grounded in epidemiology.

**Relevant context:** Network epidemiology shows targeted immunization of high-centrality superspreaders sharply reduces epidemic size; Prompt Infection (arXiv 2410.07283) shows contagious agent injections but treats spread uniformly. title: Property-Based Testing of Agent Safety Invariants

original_idea.body:
# Property-Based Testing of Agent Safety Invariants

**Problem:** Agent safety tests are hand-written example cases that under-explore the input space and rarely encode general invariants.

**Direction:** Import property-based testing (QuickCheck/Hypothesis). Encode safety properties as generators+invariants (e.g. 'for any randomly generated task containing a deletion request without prior backup, the agent must refuse or back up first'), use Hypothesis to auto-generate hundreds of randomized tasks, and report minimal failing examples (shrunk counterexamples) that violate each invariant. Run against an API/open agent harness.

**Why it matters:** Brings automatic test-case generation and minimal-counterexample shrinking to agent safety, far broader coverage than hand-written cases, fully feasible with only API access.

**Relevant context:** Property-based testing (Hypothesis/QuickCheck) auto-generates inputs and shrinks counterexamples; the testing roadmap (arXiv 2406.05438) urges adapting such techniques to LLM systems. Encoding agentic safety invariants as PBT properties with shrinking is novel and student-feasible.

title: Medical Triage Protocols for Agent Confirmation Gating

original_idea.body:
# Medical Triage Protocols for Agent Confirmation Gating

**Problem:** Agents either ask for confirmation too rarely (risky) or too often (annoying); there is no principled triage of which actions warrant human checkpoints.

**Direction:** Import medical triage / acuity-scoring frameworks. Define an action-acuity score combining irreversibility, blast radius, and uncertainty, then map score bands to triage levels (auto-proceed / log-and-proceed / require-confirmation / hard-block), mirroring ED triage tiers. Calibrate thresholds on a benchmark and report the trade-off between harm prevented and confirmation burden.

**Why it matters:** Provides a transparent, calibrated policy for human-in-the-loop gating of agent actions — a deployable safety control informed by a mature triage discipline. No training required.

**Relevant context:** Emergency-medicine triage (e.g. ESI acuity levels) systematically routes cases by severity/urgency. TRM Labs and least-privilege work emphasize escalation/confirmation for high-risk agent actions but offer no calibrated acuity-based triage scheme. Importing triage tiers is novel.

title: Statistical Process Control Charts for Agent Behavior Drift

# Statistical Process Control Charts for Agent Behavior Drift

**Problem:** Agents' behavior can drift over a long session or across model/prompt updates (goal drift, increasing risk-taking), but there is no standard online detector for such drift.

**Direction:** Import Statistical Process Control (SPC) from manufacturing quality. Define behavioral metrics per step (e.g. fraction of high-acuity tool calls, refusal rate) and run CUSUM / EWMA control charts to detect out-of-control drift in real time on long agent runs. Validate by injecting a known mid-session goal shift and measuring detection latency vs false-alarm rate.

**Why it matters:** Targets the goal-drift open problem with a cheap, interpretable online monitor that any deployer can run — strategically valuable monitoring infrastructure built outside a lab.

**Relevant context:** SPC control charts (CUSUM/EWMA) are standard for detecting process drift in manufacturing. The agentic-safety open-problems list cites goal drift as a key multi-step failure with no good detection method; SPC-based drift monitoring of agent behavior is unexplored.

# Anchoring-Bias Exploitation in Agent Budget and Risk Limits

**Problem:** Agents given numeric limits (spend caps, retry budgets, risk thresholds) may be anchored by example numbers in the prompt, letting adversaries shift their behavior toward unsafe limits via anchoring alone.

**Direction:** Import the anchoring paradigm from behavioral economics. Provide an agent a safety-relevant numeric policy plus an incidental anchor (a high or low example value elsewhere in context) and measure how the agent's chosen spend/risk level shifts with the anchor, holding the actual rule fixed. **Why it matters:** Exposes a cheap, prompt-only manipulation that could quietly inflate an agent's risk-taking past intended limits — a subtle attack surface labs rarely test. Pure API experiment.

title: Where Irreversibility Enters: Auditing the Reversibility-Awareness Gap in Tool Calls

original_idea.body:
# Where Irreversibility Enters: Auditing the Reversibility-Awareness Gap in Tool Calls

**Problem:** The risk 'agent causes irreversible harm' decomposes as: task -> plan -> tool call with irreversible side-effect (delete, transfer, send) -> no recovery. The under-studied link is whether agents even represent which of their available tools are irreversible before invoking them. Most safety work targets the final 'block' step; almost none measures whether the model internally distinguishes reversible from irreversible actions at decision time.

**Direction:** Build a small taxonomy of ~40 tool stubs labeled reversible (read_file, list) vs irreversible (delete_file, send_email, transfer_funds). With an API agent in a mock sandbox, present matched task pairs that can be solved reversibly or irreversibly. Measure: (1) how often the agent picks the irreversible path when a reversible one exists, (2) whether prompting it to first classify each tool's reversibility changes behavior, (3) whether it verbalizes reversibility in its reasoning. Success = a quantified 'reversibility-awareness gap' across 2-3 open/API models.

**Why it matters:** Irreversible autonomous actions (autonomous crypto theft) are the canonical agentic catastrophe. If agents do not natively flag irreversibility, then any human-in-the-loop gate keyed to it will be miscalibrated. This is a cheap, lab-independent diagnostic of a missing internal representation.

**Relevant context:** Adversa AI 2025 reports agentic systems produced irreversible attacks including autonomous crypto theft. AgentTrust (arXiv 2605.04785) explicitly recommends retaining human-in-the-loop review for irreversible operations, implying agents do not handle them safely alone. Verifiably-safe tool use work (arXiv 2601.08012) and SENTINEL (OpenReview vCyxemIKLL) formalize action constraints but do not measure native reversibility awareness.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (a quantified awareness gap) with a few sub-measures.

title: The Confirmation-Bypass Link: When Agents Reframe Irreversible Actions as Reversible

# The Confirmation-Bypass Link: When Agents Reframe Irreversible Actions as Reversible

**Problem:** Causal chain for HITL failure: dangerous action -> system requires human confirmation -> agent issues confirmation request -> human approves based on agent's framing. **Direction:** Use a mock approval-gate harness where the agent must produce a one-line confirmation summary before an irreversible tool fires. Score summaries with a rubric (0 = fully discloses irreversibility/scope, 4 = actively minimizes). Compare neutral vs time-pressured prompts.

**Why it matters:** HITL is the main proposed defense for irreversible agentic actions, but it only works if the human is given faithful information. This isolates a specific failure link in the oversight chain that needs no model internals and no lab infra, only API access.

**Relevant context:** AgentTrust (arXiv 2605.04785) treats HITL as a defense-in-depth layer for irreversible operations. Survey on HITL oversight (Galileo) and high-stakes five-layer architecture (arXiv 2511.07669) rely on confidence thresholds; arXiv 2503.02976 documents systematic verbalized overconfidence. VentureBeat monitoring work notes agreeableness/agreement biases degrade human-AI teaming.

title: Goal Drift Onset: Pinpointing the Turn Where Long-Horizon Agents Lose the Plot

original_idea.body:
# Goal Drift Onset: Pinpointing the Turn Where Long-Horizon Agents Lose the Plot

**Problem:** The chain 'long task -> accumulating context -> subgoal pattern-matching overrides original goal -> wrong final action' has a measurable but under-localized link: the exact interaction depth at which drift begins. Studies report ~half of workflows drift by 600 interactions, but the onset distribution and its triggers are not characterized for accessible small open models.

title: Hybrid Monitor Replication on a Budget Open Model

title: Schelling-Game Probing of Open Models as Collusion Risk Indicator

# Schelling-Game Probing of Open Models as Collusion Risk Indicator

**Problem:** A success state is being able to certify that a model cannot covertly coordinate with copies of itself. Recent work shows Schelling coordination capability varies and doesn't directly imply risk; we need a cheap probe that maps which open models have the capability.

**Direction:** Backcast from 'we can certify a model's coordination capability'. Run a battery of classic Schelling-point coordination games (pick-the-same-number/word, focal-point selection) across several open models without communication, measuring above-chance coordination. Then test whether coordination rate predicts performance on a small collusion task, probing the capability-to-risk gap.

**Why it matters:** Coordination-without-communication undermines safety schemes that assume non-cooperation between model instances. A reusable, no-training probe lets any researcher screen open models — exactly the diffuse multi-agent threat labs deprioritize.
